claims.text: Adding approximately 1–2 atomic percent yttrium to a high-entropy-alloy bond coat improves coating durability and reliability.
Yttrium doping promotes formation of a continuous, adherent oxide scale.
The oxide scale formed with yttrium doping resists spallation during high-temperature cyclic oxidation.
The untreated baseline is an undoped high-entropy-alloy bond coat of the type typically used in thermal-barrier systems.
The proposed intervention is doping the bond coat with approximately 1–2 atomic percent yttrium.
The intervention is intended to operate during cyclic oxidation above approximately 1000 °C with repeated heating and cooling.
Yttrium promotes selective oxidation in the bond coat.
Yttrium stabilizes the resulting oxide scale.
Stabilization of the oxide scale improves adhesion and reduces spallation under cyclic thermal stresses.
Yttrium doping is predicted to increase thermal-cycling lifetime by approximately 20% or more relative to an undoped bond coat tested under identical conditions.
The intervention may be less effective if the alloy lacks sufficient oxide-forming elements.
The intervention may be less effective at temperatures well above 1300 °C.
Yttrium contents above approximately 2 atomic percent may cause phase instabilities.
